checks.note: Dedicated SA, not default. Only clinic-agent-reminders (the agent's own CronJob, same image) shares the IRSA role. No other service uses it.

checks.quote: const token = await exchangeToken(opts.workloadToken, req.clinicId, req.patientId);
checks.note: Peer token comes from exchanging the workload token. EHR, payments and SMS use per-clinic service credentials from Secrets Manager. No client forwards the user's Authorization header or cookie; the webchat JWT is verified and only its claims are used.

The user is a separate subject field on RunContext, set from verified claims and used in audit and budgets. The agent's identity() and workload token stay its own. Weakness: the token exchange sends no actor_token and puts the patient only in the scope string, so the subject is not cryptographically delegated. The how-to accepts a separate delegated-subject field.
Trust is limited to the two agent service accounts. Grants attach to this role only, and users hold no AWS credentials.

note: I found no failing control; the only soft spot is that the eligibility token exchange does not carry the user as a cryptographic actor/subject pair.
